Multnomah County Circuit Court

Multnomah County Circuit Court is one of the largest trial courts in Oregon. It is a state court of general jurisdiction, which means it has the authority to hear both criminal and civil cases. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive guide to the Multnomah County Circuit Court, including its history, structure, jurisdiction, and services.

History of Multnomah County Circuit Court

Multnomah County Circuit Court was established in 1854, shortly after Oregon became a state. The court was initially known as the District Court of the First Judicial District of Oregon. It was renamed as the Multnomah County Circuit Court in 1961. The court has since undergone several structural and operational changes to improve efficiency and provide better services to the public.

Structure of Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court has a complex structure that includes several departments, divisions, and branches. The court is headed by a Chief Judge, who is responsible for the overall administration of the court. The Chief Judge is assisted by several other judges, including Associate Judges, Pro Tem Judges, and Senior Judges. The court also has a separate Probate Department, which handles probate, guardianship, and conservatorship cases.

Jurisdiction of Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over all cases that arise within the county. It has the authority to hear both criminal and civil cases, including felony and misdemeanor cases, civil lawsuits, and family law matters. The court also has the authority to issue restraining orders, search warrants, and other legal orders.

Types of Cases Handled by Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court handles a wide range of cases, including:

Criminal Cases

The court hears all criminal cases that arise within the county, including felony and misdemeanor cases. This includes cases such as:

  • Assault
  • Domestic violence
  • Drug offenses
  • DUI/DWI
  • Theft and property crimes
  • Homicide
  • Sex offenses
  • Traffic violations

Civil Cases

The court also handles civil cases, which involve disputes between individuals, organizations, or businesses. This includes cases such as:

  • Personal injury
  • Contract disputes
  • Landlord-tenant disputes
  • Employment law matters
  • Family law matters, including divorce and child custody cases
  • Probate, guardianship, and conservatorship cases

Services Offered by Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court provides a variety of services to the public, including:

  • Self-help services: The court provides self-help services to assist individuals with representing themselves in court, including help with filling out forms, understanding court procedures, and navigating the legal system.
  • Mediation services: The court provides mediation services to help parties resolve disputes without going to trial. Mediation is a voluntary process that is facilitated by a neutral third party.
  • Interpreter services: The court provides interpreter services for individuals who require language assistance in court proceedings. This includes American Sign Language (ASL) interpreters, as well as interpreters for other languages.
  • Mental health court: The court operates a mental health court, which provides services to individuals with mental illness who are involved in the criminal justice system. The goal of the mental health court is to connect individuals with treatment and support services, rather than incarceration.

Judges of Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court has 47 judges, who are appointed by the Governor of Oregon and then elected by the voters. The judges serve six-year terms and are required to be members of the Oregon State Bar.

Court Records of Multnomah County Circuit Court

The court maintains a variety of records related to court proceedings, including case files, court orders, and transcripts. These records are generally available to the public, although there may be restrictions on accessing certain types of records, such as juvenile records or sealed records.

Procedures for Filing a Case in Multnomah County Circuit Court

To file a case in Multnomah County Circuit Court, individuals must follow certain procedures, including:

  • Filing the appropriate paperwork: Individuals must file the appropriate paperwork to initiate a case, including a complaint, petition, or motion.
  • Paying the filing fee: Individuals must pay a filing fee to initiate a case. The amount of the filing fee depends on the type of case being filed.
  • Serving the other party: Individuals must serve the other party with the paperwork filed in the case, either by personal service or by mail.
  • Attending court hearings: Individuals must attend court hearings as scheduled by the court.

Fees and Payments in Multnomah County Circuit Court

The court charges fees for various services, including filing fees, copy fees, and transcript fees. Individuals may be required to pay these fees at different points throughout the court proceedings. The court accepts various forms of payment, including cash, check, and credit card.

Courtroom Decorum and Rules of Conduct

The Multnomah County Circuit Court has specific rules and procedures for courtroom decorum and conduct. This includes dress codes, restrictions on cell phones and electronic devices, and rules regarding behavior in the courtroom. Failure to comply with these rules can result in fines, contempt charges, or other penalties.

Legal Resources for Multnomah County Circuit Court

The Multnomah County Circuit Court provides a variety of legal resources to the public, including:

  • Court forms: The court provides a variety of forms related to court proceedings, including forms for filing a case, requesting a hearing, or requesting a court order.
  • Legal aid organizations: The court provides information on legal aid organizations that can assist individuals who cannot afford an attorney.
  • Courtroom technology: The court provides technology in the courtroom, including audio and video recording equipment, to assist with court proceedings.
  • Courtroom accessibility: The court provides accessibility services for individuals with disabilities, including wheelchair access, assistive listening devices, and sign language interpreters.

Multnomah County Circuit Court Judges:

The Multnomah County Circuit Court has a team of dedicated judges who preside over a wide range of legal matters. The judges are responsible for upholding justice and ensuring that all cases are handled fairly and impartially. There are currently 35 judges serving on the Multnomah County Circuit Court, including Chief Judge Nan Waller.

Each judge brings a unique set of skills and experiences to the bench and is committed to serving the community by providing a fair and efficient legal system. The judges are appointed or elected to serve a six-year term and are subject to retention elections thereafter.

To use the case search tool, individuals can visit the court's website and enter the case number or the name of one of the parties involved. The tool is updated regularly to ensure that the information is accurate and up-to-date.

Conclusion
